text:
bob_user: Hey team — streaming generator from python SDK hangs intermittently when token refresh happens. Happens ~1-2x/day on prod, client code is simple: using redwood==0.9.2.

bob_user: Minimal behavior: start stream, after ~30s auth refresh occurs (short lived 401), client resumes but generator stops yielding further tokens. No error raised, just hangs.

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste pip freeze and a small repro? Also which endpoint (text_stream/chat/generate)?

bob_user: pip freeze:
redwood==0.9.2
requests==2.31.0
Python 3.11.4
Using text_stream endpoint. Attaching truncated logs:
```
INFO: opening stream to /v1/streams/text
DEBUG: recv chunk: b'data: {"delta":"Hel'
DEBUG: recv chunk: b'lo"}\n\n'
DEBUG: recv chunk: b'data: {"delta":" Wo'
DEBUG: recv chunk: b'rld"}\n\n'
DEBUG: after 401 refresh, recv chunk: b'data: {"delta":"!','\n'
```
The third chunk after refresh looks like a partial token with an extra quote and then newline split — generator yields up to " World" then stops.

alice_support: Hmm looks like the SSE event boundary is being split mid-json after auth refresh. Can you try latest SDK (0.9.5) to see if this was already fixed? Also can you share the exact call snippet?

bob_user: Call snippet:
```
with client.stream_text(model="rwd-1.2") as gen:
    for token in gen:
        print(token.text, end="", flush=True)
```
Upgrading to 0.9.5 didn't help, still saw hang on one run. Rolling back to 0.9.1 seemed more stable but we don't have rigorous data.

cara_eng_oncall: Thanks for the repro, looping in eng oncall. @alice_support quick notes: we've seen a case where token refresh (401 -> refresh -> resume) caused the underlying requests HTTPResponse to return a fragment that splits JSON across chunk boundaries. The python SSE parser in 0.9.2 doesn't strictly buffer until a full '\n\n' event delimiter when a retry/conn-replace occurs — it tries to parse partial data and then swallows the remainder, leaving the generator waiting for more data that never arrives. Suspect two things: (1) retry logic during auth refresh concatenates buffers incorrectly, (2) edge-case where single quote/comma combos from compression/transfer-encoding split tokens.

cara_eng_oncall: Repro steps I used locally:
1) start middleware that proxies and injects a 401 mid-stream (simulate refresh).
2) server emits SSE with small JSON chunks (split words).
3) run simple client loop and observe hang.

cara_eng_oncall: Quick mitigation: ensure SDK buffers until a full '\n\n' event separator before attempting to json.loads. Here's a tiny patch we tested locally:
```
# pseudo-fix: buffer until double newline then yield
buffer += chunk.decode('utf-8')
while '\\n\\n' in buffer:
    event, buffer = buffer.split('\\n\\n', 1)
    if event.startswith('data:'):
        payload = event[len('data:'):].strip()
        yield json.loads(payload)
```
This prevents partial-token parse attempts. We'll run a full test for connection-replace cases.

dave_devex: Good find. For a short-term workaround for customers: enable `stream_keepalive` and increase SSE buffer timeout in client config to tolerate auth handoffs, or rotate to non-blocking read with a watchdog. Also, can you capture a full tcpdump of one failure so we can confirm chunk boundaries and whether proxies (NGINX) are re-chunking?

bob_user: I can run a tcpdump but need guidance on safe redaction. I'll try to reproduce in staging tomorrow and attach pcap.

alice_support: Thanks. I'll open an internal ticket and escalate to eng-runtime. For tracking: thread_ts: 1769998888 — tagging @cara_eng_oncall for PR. deploy-bot: FYI earlier incident:INC-2026-03-sse-frag might be related.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-sse-frag linked (internal), engineers investigating similar symptom on dedicated clusters.

cara_eng_oncall: Plan: (1) add stricter buffer-until-delimiter parsing to SDK, (2) add unit tests that simulate auth refresh mid-event, (3) ship patch 0.9.6 candidate and ask affected customers to test. If pcap shows intermediary re-chunking we may also add a fix in edge-proxy to avoid splitting within JSON braces.

bob_user: Thanks all — I'll try to repro in staging with tcpdump and report back. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
